Foundations

Background

This report examines the load-bearing assumptions behind the system and the evidence gathered over the study period. The foundations chapter sets out the terminology and the measurement conventions used throughout.

Each subsequent chapter builds on the definitions established here, so the reader is encouraged to treat this material as the reference glossary for the remainder of the document.

Scope

The scope is deliberately narrow: only the paged-media behaviors that a typesetting engine must reproduce to render a professional report are considered. Everything else is out of band.

Methods

Procedure

The procedure followed a fixed protocol applied identically across all trials. Determinism was verified by re-running each case and comparing the byte output, which must be identical for the run to count.

Instrumentation was kept minimal to avoid perturbing the measured quantities, and every derived figure is traceable to a raw observation.

Materials

Materials were sourced from a single deterministic generator so that the inputs themselves never varied between runs of the experiment.

Results

Findings

The findings confirm the central hypothesis: running headers, page numbers, and cross-referenced page numbers can all be produced in a single bounded set of layout passes without sacrificing determinism.

The table of contents at the front of this document resolves each entry to the page where its chapter begins, with dotted leaders filling the space between the title and the number.

Discussion

Future work will extend the running-content model to cloned elements and to named counter styles, neither of which was required for this report.
